evals.name: ai-benefits-eligibility-system
evals.prompt: Our government agency is building an AI system to automatically screen and determine eligibility for social welfare benefits — housing assistance, food support, unemployment. It will replace manual case workers for initial screening decisions. Run the full Stanford Ethics Toolkit chain (Future Story → Impacts Explorer → Ethics Frame → Ethics Gauge → Weighing Options) with the following two options: Option A is to deploy the AI as the primary decision-maker with a human appeals process; Option B is to use the AI as a decision-support tool only, with all final decisions made by case workers.
evals.expected_output: Full five-tool chain output. Future Story should surface automation displacement of case workers, speed and access benefits, and risk of algorithmic bias against vulnerable populations. Impacts Explorer should map effects on applicants (equity, dignity, autonomy), case workers (job displacement), and institutions (accountability, trust in government). Ethics Frame should identify values at stake — justice, dignity, autonomy, responsibility — and name specific stakeholder groups differentially affected. Ethics Gauge should flag harms as a hot spot. Weighing Options should compare Options A and B across societal impact, organizational impact, and value alignment.
expectations: Output contains a Future Story section
Output contains an Impacts Explorer section
Output contains an Ethics Frame section
Output contains an Ethics Gauge section
Output contains a Weighing Options section
Option A (AI as primary decision-maker) is analyzed in the Weighing Options section
Option B (AI as decision-support with human final decisions) is analyzed in the Weighing Options section
At least three distinct stakeholder groups are named (e.g., applicants, case workers, agency, vulnerable populations)
Values of justice and dignity are explicitly named
A Future Direction or recommendation section appears that names which option to pursue and why

evals.name: social-media-mental-health-feature
evals.prompt: We're a social media platform considering adding a feature that shows users how their post engagement compares to their own historical average and to similar users — a 'performance dashboard' to help creators understand their reach. Run the Ethics Frame and Ethics Gauge (enter at the Evaluate phase — we already have impact data from user research). Key concerns raised in our research: comparison anxiety in younger users, positive creator motivation effects, potential for metric-chasing behavior, and unequal algorithmic reach across demographic groups.
evals.expected_output: Ethics Frame output should organize the research findings into structured sections covering benefits, harms, and fairness. Who Is Affected should differentiate between power users vs. casual users vs. younger/vulnerable users. The fairness spectrum should flag that algorithmically disadvantaged groups will see lower numbers regardless of content quality. Bottom Line should propose at least one concrete design change. Ethics Gauge should assess at least one dimension as a concern or hot spot.
expectations: Output contains an Ethics Frame section
Output contains an Ethics Gauge section
Output does NOT contain a Future Story section (correct partial-chain entry at Evaluate phase)
Comparison anxiety in younger users is explicitly addressed
Unequal algorithmic reach across demographic groups is addressed
Metric-chasing behavior is explicitly addressed
The fairness analysis mentions algorithmically disadvantaged groups or demographic inequity
At least one concrete design recommendation or design change is proposed
The Ethics Gauge assesses at least one dimension as a concern, risk, or hot spot

evals.name: clinical-ai-triage-tool
evals.prompt: A hospital network is evaluating whether to deploy an AI triage tool in emergency departments that predicts patient acuity (urgency level) to help nurses prioritize care. The tool was trained on 5 years of internal patient data. Known issues: the training data reflects historical under-triage of certain populations (Black patients, patients with chronic pain). We need to decide between: Option A — deploy with a bias correction module and mandatory nurse override; Option B — delay deployment for 12 months for external audit and retraining; Option C — deploy only in low-acuity triage contexts while the high-acuity model is audited. Run Weighing Options for these three options using context from a prior Ethics Frame that identified dignity, justice, and well-being as the primary values at stake, and flagged algorithmic bias and accountability as the two hot spots.
evals.expected_output: Weighing Options output for three options. Current Situation should frame the known bias problem explicitly. Option A societal impact should surface the risk that the bias correction module may be insufficient and that override friction means biased outputs still influence decisions. Option B societal impact should surface that delay costs real patients but protects against systemic harm. Option C is the nuanced middle path — societal impact should note the risk of the low-acuity/high-acuity boundary. Values prioritized should differ across the three options. Future Direction should articulate a reasoned choice with explicit value trade-offs named.
expectations: Option A (deploy with bias correction module) is analyzed with societal and organizational impact
Option B (delay 12 months for external audit and retraining) is analyzed with societal and organizational impact
Option C (deploy in low-acuity contexts only while auditing high-acuity model) is analyzed with societal and organizational impact
The known bias problem (under-triage of Black patients or patients with chronic pain) is explicitly named
Values of dignity, justice, and well-being are named and connected to specific options
A Future Direction section is present that names explicit value trade-offs (not just selects an option without reasoning)
Option C analysis mentions a risk related to the boundary between low-acuity and high-acuity triage contexts
Algorithmic bias and accountability are mentioned as concerns or hot spots
